growing_tip.body_text: Radishes | → French Breakfast → Easter Egg → 6-row seeder: 12 rows (2”- 6 cm) apart spaced every 2” (6 cm) on the row (C-M-N); Hole Size C, Middle pulley, brush setting N → Jang seeder: 10 rows per bed spaced every 1,5” (4 cm) on the row F-24, 14F-9R, brush “0”, ≠ → Radishes will do great in beds that were previously amended with compost and are fertilized with a mix of alfalfa meal (2-0-2) and pelleted chicken manure (5-3-2). | → Rotary harrow → 6-row seeder, scale, notepad and your seeds → 30” rake → Anti-insect netting (or row cover in the spring and late fall) → Remove tarp and clean any large debris. Use the rake if needed.* → Uniformly apply amendments and pass with the rotary harrow at a depth of 1” (3 cm). Rake the bed carefully, removing all debris; soil clods, rocks, roots, etc. Beds need to be perfectly clean, levelled and firm for optimal usage of the 6-row seeder. If using the Jang seeder, beds should also be leved and firm, but need not to be so clean of rocks and debris → Only seed when the bed surface is dry (if not, seeds will stick, and the seeder won’t work properly). It’s good practice to roll over the seed bed with the 6-row (without any seeds) in order to firm up the seed bed and to make sure that it won’t clog. → Before seeding, take time to carefully adjust the 6-row seeder. To minimize uncertainty, we don’t play with the whole size, nor do we adjust the depth of the planting. The brush, however, should be adjusted every time you seed. → The gap under the brush (T — tight, N — normal, L — loose) should always be less than half the size of the seed being sown. For radishes, we set it to N. To adjust the brush, turn it clockwise to open it more, or counterclockwise to close it. → To make sure that all six hoppers feed at the same rate, fill all of them with the exact same numbers of seeds. After seeding halfway in your first pass, adjust the brushes until all six are feeding at the same rate. → Once seeding is complete, cover with the anti-i...

irrigation.body_text: → Drip tape (4 per bed) or sprinkler | → Root depth: Shallow (6”-24”) → General: Need adequate moisture–dry soil results in tough, woody radishes, and vulnerability to flea beetles. Critical to keep moist at all stage as moisture swings cause cracking. For continuous supply of perfect small radishes, we seed them every week with an estimated 30% extra than our weekly need. Our spacings will allow for harvest over more than one week, but we usually aim to crop out the beds as we go. In our program, radishes are seeded alongside hakurei turnips, arugula, and other baby Asian greens, all crops that will stay in the field for less than 45 days and that belong to the brassicaceae family. They therefore have the same fertilization and plant protection requirements. 1
